findings.evidence: Every row sets source_basis='self_reported'. Primary evidence SOURCE 1 and SOURCEs 7-20 are ARC Prize, Inc.'s Verified Leaderboard v2.json entries, and SOURCE 3 (ARC Prize Verified Testing Policy) states the Foundation itself runs evaluations and publishes results. These are independently measured/verified ARC Prize scores, not model self-reports. Labelling them self_reported misstates the basis required by criterion c1.
findings.repair: Set source_basis to 'measured' (or 'third_party_measured') on all 15 rows, retaining basis='derived' for the unit conversion.
Recompute each derived value by exact decimal scaling (multiply source decimal by 100 without additional floating error) and make derivation.inputs agree with the emitted value.

findings.evidence: subject.variant and subject.harness are null on every row. SOURCE 3 policy explicitly states ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 evaluations are direct input→output predictors with no agent harness and no client-side tools. Criterion c1 requires explicitly published effort/harness to be verified; the reasoning effort is only embedded in modelId/name suffixes (max/xhigh/high/medium/low/none), not in a structured effort field, and the no-harness condition is not represented.
findings.repair: Record the effort explicitly (e.g., populate subject.variant from the modelId suffix) and set subject.harness to 'none' or 'stateless direct' per the published ARC-AGI-2 testing policy, or document that no harness applies.

uncertainties: I cannot execute SHA-256, transport, hashing or qualification checks; those are owner-run and not independently verified here.
Tiny numeric differences (~1e-14) may reflect IEEE-754 arithmetic; I still flag them because criterion c1 says exact primary value.
Policy pages are supplied as exact excerpts; I did not compare full page content beyond the provided bounds.
